motion.name: landing-master-timeline
motion.value: Paused Anime.js timeline; 4-unit SVG draw and 32 by 22-unit code packet motion path; five scroll chapters
motion.purpose: Native scroll seeks a paused Anime.js timeline across five 1000ms windows. svg.createDrawable draws the delivery line at 4 SVG units over a 2.5-unit guide; svg.createMotionPath supplies the coordinates of a centered 32 by 22 SVG-unit coral code packet with a native bracket glyph. The packet and path share one SVG viewBox. Checkpoint labels sit 15px below the path to clear the packet. Connect joins four sources. Trace follows the original build, passing tests and release error. Understand returns to the test checkpoint; Investigate returns to the related pull request; Automate follows the evidence into a review request. Reverse scrolling retraces the same path. Frame-rate-independent damping uses 1 - exp(-delta * 12), capped at 0.05 seconds, and stops at rest, outside the story and in hidden tabs. ResizeObserver tracks the scene and story to preserve chapter synchronization when previews change height. Native HTML checkpoint controls remain available throughout.

motion.name: landing-workflow-playback
motion.value: User-initiated Anime.js animation; 2400ms; linear; four selected steps
motion.purpose: Illustrative forward delivery and reverse investigation update tool explanations. The play button disables during playback; reduced motion selects the terminal step.

motion.name: landing-text-sequence
motion.value: Persistent Anime.js splitText; reversible scroll-driven entrance, reading interval and exit; out(3) / in(2)
motion.purpose: Anime.js splitText keeps clipped heading characters and explanatory words split throughout the tour. A paused timeline has an entrance, a reading interval and an exit; native scroll geometry continuously seeks its position with frame-rate-independent damping, so both directions animate smoothly. Heading entrances use 540 timeline milliseconds plus at most 180 of stagger; explanatory words begin at 120 and use 400 plus at most 200 of stagger. Heading exits begin at 900 with 320 plus at most 180 of stagger; explanatory exits begin at 950 with 280 plus at most 150 of stagger. Chapter evidence metadata shares the timeline, entering with its explanation and exiting with it. These are timeline positions, not a fixed playback duration: scrolling controls the sequence. Investigate reverses the heading travel direction. The first visible passage, including the hero, animates in on initialization. A reading interval accounts for paragraph height, and focusing a visible passage reveals its text. Resize reflows the persistent word wrappers and recalculates scroll thresholds. Frames stop at rest and in hidden tabs. Reduced motion and unmount revert timelines and splits to the original static text; cleanup also removes frames, observers and listeners. Server-rendered text remains readable before initialization or without JavaScript.

motion.name: landing-static-fallback
motion.value: Server-rendered SVG; static line and instant updates for reduced motion
motion.purpose: The same labeled SVG, text, code and native anchors are server-rendered and readable without JavaScript. Reduced motion shows the complete line and updates the story immediately without animated travel or text splitting. WebGL is not required. The follower stays within the SVG coordinate system when resized. Native checkpoint buttons expose source-specific names, pressed states and keyboard focus. Unmount cancels animation frames, reverts timelines and removes observers and listeners. Live preference changes are supported.

narrative.overview:
Forge uses neutral charcoal surfaces, fine gray rules, compact controls, and readable operational detail. The approved dark developer-tool brief is the visual authority. Color communicates state; typography and spacing establish hierarchy.

This document records the implemented Phase 1 foundation and Phase 2 workspace access in `apps/web`: the protected overview, account creation and sign-in, email verification and password recovery, team invitations, organization onboarding and switching, organization settings, membership roles, activity, and session revocation. System status and the setup guide remain public. Provider integrations, engineering metrics, and charts remain future work.

The public landing page at `/` follows one illustrative checkout commit along a centered SVG path. Anime.js draws a 4-unit line between GitHub, Actions, JUnit and Sentry logos and moves a coral code packet with an authored bracket glyph along it. The packet traces delivery, returns to the regression test and related code, then ends at a human review request. Headings and explanations animate into view, stay readable through a reading interval and animate out as the visitor scrolls on. Scrolling back reverses the same sequence. Each chapter retains its realistic code preview. The Anime.js palette remains warm charcoal, off-white, coral controls and warm stone integrations. The application retains its compact neutral foundation. The wordmark remains; a future 3D logo is deferred.
keyCharacteristics: Flat charcoal surfaces with subtle borders.
Geist interface text with system monospace for commands and versions.
Restrained controls and explicit, text-supported service states.
Responsive navigation and locally scrollable technical content.
Persistent form labels, visible access roles, and divided settings sections.
A scoped public landing with a continuous delivery track, tool checkpoints and five code examples.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use state colors with a label and icon. An unverified or loading check must remain visually distinct from a healthy check.

dos: **Do** use subtle borders and tonal separation for operational surfaces.
**Do** pair state color with explicit text and an icon.
**Do** preserve unknown, checking, unavailable, and healthy as distinct states.
**Do** keep mobile technical content locally scrollable with a visible cue when needed.
**Do** use real navigation targets and neutral descriptions of health checks.
**Do** scope the warm charcoal and coral page palette, source colors, display typography, SVG path drawing and checkpoint transitions to the public marketing surface.
**Do** keep the static delivery track, chapter content, and native navigation available with reduced motion or JavaScript disabled.
donts: **Don't** fabricate metrics, customer data, connected sources, or working planned controls.
**Don't** replace the restrained application foundation with the landing's material gradients, depth, or oversized display text.
**Don't** treat a healthy installation as evidence that an engineering source is connected.
**Don't** document future provider connections, metrics, or charts as implemented patterns.
